Senses.Explanation: The Land of Bliss soundscape — water-birds and tree-groves — ruled at the root over Dongshan's insentient-preaching question, then roared from staff-heads, sheared from litanies, and swapped for eyes across nine centuries of halls and odes. The root sits in Yunyan Tansheng's own answer, carried in the true-eye storehouse: Dongshan asks what canonical teaching the insentient preaching belongs to, and Yunyan answers: do you not see the Amitabha sutra — water-birds and tree-groves, all of them minding the buddha, minding the teaching; the insentient grasses and trees playing reed-pipes to each other — and Dongshan woke partway there, oding: how utterly strange, the insentient preaching unthinkable; try to hear it with the ear and it will never meet you — sound known at the eye is the only way; Huangbo Xiyun, in the Wanling record, folds it into the never-silent: speech is silence, silence is speech, the sound's own true nature never cut off; the thus-come always speaks, never a time of not-speaking — the teaching is the speaking, the speaking the teaching — down to the reward-body and the transformation-body, the voice-hearers, mountains and rivers, the great earth, water-birds and tree-groves, all preaching at once: speaking in speech and speaking in silence, all day speaking and never once having spoken — and so, take silence for the root; Baiyun Shouduan, in the five-house praises: as I press my finger, the ocean-seal gives off its light — the staff lifted, and mountains, rivers, the great earth, water-birds and tree-groves, the sentient and the insentient, all making the great lion's roar atop the staff-head, preaching the great perfection of wisdom; and Xiaoyin Daxin, at the great report-lands temple, sets the two lands against each other — the Land of Bliss, where water-birds and tree-groves all mind the buddha; the Contentment heaven, where trees brushing together preach the bitter and the empty — then the whisk raised: this mountain monk's whisk threads your nostrils — where will you breathe out? Tianyin Yuanxiu, oding the very question Dongshan asked: water-birds and tree-groves all mind the teaching — what sentient being cannot hear it and understand?; sunk through ten thousand kalpas and suddenly awake: every thing, every head, always already complete; Shanhui Huan shears the litany apart — seal mind with mind and mind has no such mind; hand the teaching on and the teaching has no such teaching: mountains and rivers are their own mountains and rivers, the ten thousand forms their own ten thousand forms, water-birds and tree-groves their own water-birds and tree-groves, the sage-and-commoner measure its own measure, fine words their own fine words, staff and shout their own staff and shout — the whole heap of them nothing to do with me — and the staff knocks once: the yaksha draws its sword and stirs the dragon-gate, a thousand fathoms, ten thousand fathoms, shaking the sea; and Shiyu Mingfang, at the Baoshou hall: before you stepped over the boat's gunwale, one Baoshou had already been inscribed on your mind-source; all the way here — dressing, eating, talking, laughing — each a single Baoshou, not high, not low, not big, not small; and then on arrival, the water-birds and tree-groves, the bells, chimes, gongs and drums went and swapped your eyes; they never left Baoshou — but can you hear the water-birds and tree-groves all minding buddha, minding teaching, minding the order?; the old worthies' line — with the ear you will never meet it; known in the eye at last — so tell me: how does the eye hear? how does the eye see?
